finding_dispositions.note: Alleluia added to the first reading's opening statement, a new paragraph in its retitled subsection on the way and the will of God (with the Collect paragraph), and its moral and anagogical senses; witnesses credited only with what they say of the verse.

Comparison's first paragraph split into what all three hold (Postcommunion answering the Introit, the Introit's confession heard three ways, the Communion's hope) and partial ground credited by reading; last paragraph now says the second reading does not treat et credidit ipse and reports what it does say of the Gospel.

summary: Repaired the two blocking study findings and the advisory: the first reading now gives the Alleluia a place in its thesis, argument (Augustine and Bellarmine on Ps 56:8, Schuster on gloria mea, Cassiodorus on Ps 107:2, every join to the Gospel marked as the editor's) and moral and anagogical senses; the comparison claims as common only what all three readings hold and credits each other feature to the readings that hold it, with the second reading's supporting use of the Gospel described and its invented account of the Gospel's last words replaced; the scope appendix's commentator clause matches the study's use.
